title: Preoperative anaemia pathways for elective hip and knee replacement: a scoping review to design a referral pathway
subtitle: Mapping referral triggers, screening points, leadership, treatment access and waiting times
statement: A regional orthopaedic centre performing about 1,900 elective hip and knee replacements a year finds anaemia in about one patient in six at pre-assessment, too late for treatment, and postponed 41 operations for anaemia last year. It plans a preoperative anaemia clinic with a referral pathway but lacks agreement on where to screen, which values trigger referral, who runs the clinic and how distant patients get intravenous iron. A scoping review of how such pathways are organised elsewhere will inform the design.
whoAffected: Adults awaiting elective hip or knee replacement, especially those with anaemia and those living far from the centre; surgeons, anaesthetists, pre-assessment nurses and primary care.
whatHurts: Late detection leaves no time for treatment, so patients have surgery with anaemia or face short-notice postponement, with more pain and worry while they wait.
currentPractice: Screening at pre-assessment three to four weeks before surgery; no anaemia clinic; ad hoc arrangements for intravenous iron.
whyNow: Funding agreed in principle and a planning committee decision due in May 2027.
constraints: No research funding; two anaesthesia residents for about 60 hours each between November 2026 and April 2027; the pathway design must be ready for the hospital's planning committee in May 2027.
patientCenteredGoal: Patients arrive for joint replacement with anaemia treated in time, without avoidable postponement or long journeys.
summary: Problem framed as a scoping review of preoperative anaemia pathways to design a local referral pathway.
